prompt.context: The maker of Botox is considering expanding to the migraine market and has already begun clinical trials in this area. The product is expected to receive FDA approval in 2019. Your team has been hired to assess the viability of this product for launch.
prompt.question: How will you determine if the market is attractive? If the market is attractive, do you have any recommendations regarding how to launch the product? What concerns should the client take into consideration before deciding to launch?

clarifying_info.q: What is the price of the drug?
clarifying_info.a: The drug will be priced at $200 per injection.
Remaining development and launch costs amount to approximately $5B. Manufacturing marginal costs are expected to be quite small. Annual marketing expense can be estimated at $1B.

The product is a prophylactic injection given every 2 months. It offers similar efficacy compared to the market leading option but without any side effects. When taken for migraines it does have some added skin care benefits.
The market leading branded prescription oral migraine treatment lost patent protection last year. There is also a strong over-the-counter generic market for migraine treatments.

clarifying_info.q: What geography should we focus on?
clarifying_info.a: This drug will initially be produced in the US, so use US population of 320 million.

framework: Market sizing: Estimate the size of the US migraine prescription market (patient population, revenue potential, Botox market share)
Profitability assessment: Compare projected revenues against development, launch, and marketing costs
Launch considerations: Evaluate branding, cannibalization, competition, regulatory, and patient adoption risks
Recommendation: Synthesize findings into a go/no-go recommendation with key risks and next steps

questions.prompt: Estimate the potential annual revenue Botox could generate from the migraine indication.
questions.guidance: Candidate should use a top-down market sizing approach: US population → % chronic migraine sufferers → % severe (prescription-worthy) → Botox market share → revenue per patient per year. Challenge the candidate to justify each assumption.

math.setup: US population × % chronic migraine sufferers × % severe sufferers = total addressable patients; multiply by annual revenue per patient and Botox market share to get Botox annual revenue.
steps: % with chronic migraines: ~15% (1 in 7 ≈ 14.3%, rounded to 15%) → 320M × 15% = 48M chronic sufferers
% who are severe and seek prescription treatment: 25% → 48M × 25% = 12M patients
Price per injection: $200; injections per year: 12 months ÷ 2 months = 6
Botox market share: 30% (justified by no side effects and skin care benefits) → $14.4B × 30% = $4.32B

questions.prompt: What concerns should the client take into consideration before deciding to launch?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate structures concerns into buckets: Branding, Cannibalization/Erosion, Competition/Formulary, Regulatory, and Patient Adoption. The interviewer should challenge the candidate to justify each concern.

brainstorming.prompt: What concerns should the client take into consideration before deciding to launch Botox in the migraine indication?

categories.name: Branding
ideas: The Botox brand carries a specific and somewhat controversial cosmetic image, which may reduce patients' willingness to use it for a non-cosmetic indication
Having both products under the same brand increases risk exposure: an adverse event in the larger migraine market could damage the existing cosmetic market

categories.name: Cannibalization / Erosion
ideas: If physicians and consumers recognize the two products are essentially the same compound, it will be difficult to maintain separate markets
Launching at a much lower price point than the cosmetic indication could cause off-label usage and price erosion in the cosmetic segment

categories.name: Competition / Formulary
ideas: Given only comparable efficacy versus generics, insurance companies may decline to put the Botox migraine treatment on formulary
Many migraine sufferers may be unable to afford the treatment out-of-pocket if not covered by insurance

categories.name: Regulatory
ideas: Launching a new indication of an existing product can be challenging; FDA may require different labeling and restrict the product to certain specialties, requiring separate marketing efforts

categories.name: Patient Adoption
ideas: Patients tend to be averse to injectable therapies, particularly when comparable oral treatments are available
Targeting a specific high-efficacy patient subpopulation may improve adoption and justify the injectable format

categories.name: Geographic Expansion
ideas: The client could submit for approval in other countries to increase the potential market size beyond the US

recommendation: The projected prescription migraine market ($14.4B total, $4.32B Botox share) represents a large and attractive opportunity with significant revenue and profit potential
However, significant challenges exist under the company's proposed strategy, including cannibalization of the highly profitable cosmetic Botox product
Launching under a separate brand name would allow the client to more effectively differentiate between the two uses, price the products independently, and reduce cross-contamination risk
risks: Regulatory: FDA approval for the new indication is not yet secured; launch is contingent on this
Branding: Using the same brand name risks reputational damage if adverse events occur in the larger migraine market; using a different name risks insufficient market traction
Cannibalization: Launching at a lower price point may drive significant off-label use and erode margins in the cosmetic segment
next_steps: Continue clinical trials and obtain FDA approval for the migraine indication
Establish regulatory, branding, and marketing-based barriers between the cosmetic and migraine markets
Set up contracts with insurance companies to ensure formulary coverage for the Botox migraine product prior to launch
